title: Rama bids farewell to his birth-place
introduction: Rama bids farewell to his birth-place Ayodhya and reaches the bank of the holy Ganga. There, Nishadas offers welcome reception to Rama and others.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अयोध्य काण्डे पञ्चाशः सर्गः
Thus completes 50th chapter in the AyodhyaKanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
विशालान् कोसलान् रम्यान् यात्वा लक्ष्मण पूर्वजः |
अयोध्याभिमुखो धीमान् प्राञ्ञ्लिर्वाक्वमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
viśālān kosalān ramyān yātvā lakṣmaṇa pūrvajaḥ |
ayodhyābhimukho dhīmān prāJṇJṇlirvākvamabravīt
verses.translation: Having traveled the extensive and beautiful Kosala territory and standing with his face turned towards Ayodhya, the wise Rama with joined palms spoke the following words:

glosses.meaning: and standing with his face turned towards Ayodhya

verses.devanagari:
आपृच्छे त्वाम् पुरीश्रेष्ठे काकुत्स्थपरिपालिते |
दैवतानि च यानि त्वाम् पालयन्त्यावसन्ति च
verses.iast:
āpṛcche tvām purīśreśhṭhe kākutsthaparipālite |
daivatāni ca yāni tvām pālayantyāvasanti ca
verses.translation: "I bid farewell to you, Oh best of the cities, carefully protected by Dasaratha born in Kakutstha dynasty, as well as of the deities who protect you and dwell in you."

glosses.meaning: ruled by Dasaratha born in kakutstha dynasty! aapR^ichchhe = I bid farewell

verses.devanagari:
निवृत्तवनवासस्त्वामनृणो जगतीपतेः |
पुनर्ध्रक्ष्यामि मात्रा च पित्रा च सह सम्गतः
verses.iast:
nivṛttavanavāsastvāmanṛṇo jagatīpateḥ |
punardhrakśyāmi mātrā ca pitrā ca saha samgataḥ
verses.translation: "After getting relieved from exile in the forest and thus freed from the debt to the emperor, I shall see you again, duly getting united with my mother and father."

glosses.meaning: after getting relieved from dwelling in the forest

verses.devanagari:
ततो रुधिरताम्राक्षो भुजमुद्यम्य दक्षिणम् |
अश्रुपूर्णमुखो दीनोऽब्रवीज्जानपदम् जनम्
verses.iast:
tato rudhiratāmrākśo bhujamudyamya dakśiṇam |
aśrupūrṇamukho dīno'bravījjānapadam janam
verses.translation: Lifting his right arm and wearing a woeful look, his face covered with tears, Rama possessing lovely reddish eyes, spoke them to the people hailing from the countryside.(as follows) :

glosses.meaning: and who was having lovely reddish eyes

verses.devanagari:
अनुक्रोशो दया चैव यथार्हम् मयि वह् कृतः |
चिरम् दुःखस्य पापीयो गम्यतामर्थसिद्धये
verses.iast:
anukrośo dayā caiva yathārham mayi vah kṛtaḥ |
ciram duḥkhasya pāpīyo gamyatāmarthasiddhaye
verses.translation: "Mercy and compassion according to my worth (in your view) have been shown to me by you. Keeping agony for a long time is undesirable. Let each return to accomplish your desired object(attending to your house-hold work)!"

glosses.meaning: is miserable. gamyataam = Let you be gone
for accomplishing your desired object (viz. attending to your house-hold work)."

verses.devanagari:
तेऽभिवाद्य महात्मानम् कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम् |
विलपन्तो नरा घोरम् व्यतिष्ठन्त क्वचित् क्वचित्
verses.iast:
te'bhivādya mahātmānam kṛtvā cāpi pradakśiṇam |
vilapanto narā ghoram vyatiśhṭhanta kvacit kvacit
verses.translation: Respectfully saluting the high soled prince and going round him clockwise (as a mark of reverence), those men stood rooted here and there, wailing frightfully.

glosses.meaning: and going round him clockwise (as a mark of respect)

verses.devanagari:
तथा विलपताम् तेषामतृप्तानाम् च राघवः |
अचक्षुरिषयम् प्रायाद्यथार्कः क्षणदामुखे
verses.iast:
tathā vilapatām teśhāmatṛptānām ca rāghavaḥ |
acakśuriśhayam prāyādyathārkaḥ kśaṇadāmukhe
verses.translation: While they were lamenting thus unceasingly, Rama passed beyond their sight, as the sun sinks out of view at nightfall.

verses.devanagari:
ततो धान्यधनोपेतान् दानशीलजनान् शिवान् |
अकुतश्चिद्भयान् रम्याम् श्चैत्ययूपसमावृतान्
उद्यानाम्रवनोपेतान् सम्पन्नसलिलाशयान् |
तुष्टपुष्टजनाकीर्णान् गोकुलाकुलसेवितान्
लक्षणीयान्न रेंद्राणाम् ब्रह्मघोषाभिनादितान् |
रथेन पुरुषव्याघ्रः कोसलानत्यवर्तत
verses.iast:
tato dhānyadhanopetān dānaśīlajanān śivān |
akutaścidbhayān ramyām ścaityayūpasamāvṛtān
udyānāmravanopetān sampannasalilāśayān |
tuśhṭapuśhṭajanākīrṇān gokulākulasevitān
lakśaṇīyānna reṃdrāṇām brahmaghośhābhināditān |
rathena puruśhavyāghraḥ kosalānatyavartata
verses.translation: Then Rama, a tiger among men, in his chariot, crossed Kosala territory, which was rich in grain and treasure, inhabited by men given to charity, benevolent and free from every danger, pleasing, full of temples and sacrificial stakes, adorned with gardens and mango-orchards, intersected by ponds full of water, populated by contented and well nourished people, abounded in herds of cows which deserved to be seen by all kings and which re-echoed to the chanting of religious texts.

glosses.meaning: which was rich in grain and treasure
inhabited by men given to charity
benevolent and free from every danger
full of temples and sacrificial stakes
adorned with gardens and mango orchards
intersected by ponds full of water
which deserved to be seen by
and which re- echoed to the charity of religious texts.

verses.devanagari:
मध्येन मुदितम् स्फीतम् रम्योद्यानसमाकुलम् |
राज्यम् भोग्यम् नरेन्द्राणाम् ययौ धृतिमताम् वरः
verses.iast:
madhyena muditam sphītam ramyodyānasamākulam |
rājyam bhogyam narendrāṇām yayau dhṛtimatām varaḥ
verses.translation: Rama, the best among the resolute, moved into the middle of a happy and prosperous kingdom, abounding in lovely gardens and fit to be enjoyed by kings.

verses.devanagari:
तत्र त्रिपथगाम् दिव्याम् शिव तोयाम् अशैवलाम् |
ददर्श राघवो गन्गाम् पुण्याम् ऋषि निसेविताम्
verses.iast:
tatra tripathagām divyām śiva toyām aśaivalām |
dadarśa rāghavo gangām puṇyām ṛṣi nisevitām
verses.translation: There, Rama beheld the celestial and lovely river of Ganga with its tree tributaries, carrying clear waters without green moss and frequented by sages.

glosses.meaning: which takes a three fold course (through three tributaries) ramyaam = a lovely one

verses.devanagari:
आश्रमैरविदूर्स्थैः श्रीमद्भिः समलम् कृताम् |
कालेऽप्सरोभिर्हृष्टाभिः सेविताम्भोह्रदाम् शिवाम्
verses.iast:
āśramairavidūrsthaiḥ śrīmadbhiḥ samalam kṛtām |
kāle'psarobhirhṛśhṭābhiḥ sevitāmbhohradām śivām
verses.translation: The River Ganga was adorned with splendid hermitages within easy distance from one another, with pools overflowing with water, visited at suitable hours by celestial nymphs thrilling with rapture.

glosses.meaning: with pools overflowing with water visited

verses.devanagari:
देवदानवगन्धर्वैः किन्नरैरुपशोभिताम् |
नागगन्धर्वपत्नीभिः सेविताम् सततम् शिवाम्
verses.iast:
devadānavagandharvaiḥ kinnarairupaśobhitām |
nāgagandharvapatnībhiḥ sevitām satatam śivām
verses.translation: The blessed river was graced by gods and demons, Gandharvas(celestial musicians) and kinnaras and was constantly visited by consorts of Nagas and Gandharvas.

verses.devanagari:
देवाक्रीडशताकीर्णाम् देवोद्यानशतायुताम् |
देवार्थमाकाशगमाम् विख्याताम् देवपद्मिनीम्
verses.iast:
devākrīḍaśatākīrṇām devodyānaśatāyutām |
devārthamākāśagamām vikhyātām devapadminīm
verses.translation: The well known river was hemmed in by hills serving as the play- ground of hundreds of celestials and embellished with hundreds of celestial gardens; it coursed through the heavens for the benefit of gods and which in heaven was named "The stream of Golden Lotuses".

glosses.meaning: the hills serving as the playground of hundreds of celestials
embellished with hundreds of celestial gardens

verses.devanagari:
जलघाताट्टहासोग्राम् फेननिर्मलहासिनीम् |
क्वचिद्वेणीकृतजलाम् क्वचिदावर्तशोभिताम्
verses.iast:
jalaghātāṭṭahāsogrām phenanirmalahāsinīm |
kvacidveṇīkṛtajalām kvacidāvartaśobhitām
verses.translation: The holy river, the sound of whose clashing waves and its striking with rocks resembled a deep laughter, having a bright smile as white as a foam, its waters reduced at some places to the shape of a maiden's plaited locks, was rendered beautiful at some places by whirl pools.

glosses.meaning: the sound of whose clashing waves and striking with rocks resembles deep laughter
having a smile as white as a foam
its water reduced to the shape of a maiden's plaited locks

verses.devanagari:
क्वचित्स्तिमितगम्भीराम् क्वचिद्वेगजलाकुलाम् |
क्वचिद्गम्भीरनिर्घोषाम् क्वचिद्भैरवनिस्वनाम्
verses.iast:
kvacitstimitagambhīrām kvacidvegajalākulām |
kvacidgambhīranirghośhām kvacidbhairavanisvanām
verses.translation: At some places, its waters were still and deep. At some places, they were disturbed with violent agitation. At some places, they made a deep roaring sound. At some places, they were having a terrific noise

glosses.meaning: its waters were still and deep
they were disturbed with violent agitation

verses.devanagari:
देवसम्घाप्लुतजलाम् निर्मलोत्पलशोभिताम् |
क्वचिदाभोगपुलिनाम् क्वचिन्नर्मलवालुकाम्
verses.iast:
devasamghāplutajalām nirmalotpalaśobhitām |
kvacidābhogapulinām kvacinnarmalavālukām
verses.translation: Hosts of gods took a dip into its water .It was adorned by white lotuses. It was hemmed in, with expanse of small islands and at some places, lined with white sands.

glosses.meaning: hosts of gods took a dip into its water

verses.devanagari:
हंस सरस सम्घुष्टाम् चक्र वाक उपकूजिताम् |
सदामदैश्च विहगैरभिसम्नादिताम् तराम्
verses.iast:
haṃsa sarasa samghuṣṭām cakra vāka upakūjitām |
sadāmadaiśca vihagairabhisamnāditām tarām
verses.translation: The river was rendered resonant by swans and cranes, was graced with cackling of Chakrawaka** birds and other birds which are in rut all through the year kept hovering on its water.

glosses.meaning: rendered resonant by swans and cranes
which are in rut all through
kept hovering in its middle. **-Chakravaka is a species of bird

verses.devanagari:
क्वचित्तीररुहैर्वृक्षैर्मालाभिरिव शोभिताम् |
क्वचित्फुल्लोत्पलच्छन्नाम् क्वचित्पद्मवनाकुलाम्
verses.iast:
kvacittīraruhairvṛkśairmālābhiriva śobhitām |
kvacitphullotpalacchannām kvacitpadmavanākulām
verses.translation: At some places the river was adorned with trees growing on its banks encircling like garlands, at some places crowded with thick cluster of lotuses.

glosses.meaning: crowded with thick cluster of lotuses.

verses.devanagari:
क्वचित्कुमुदष्ण्डैश्च कुड्मलैरुपशोभिताम् |
नानापुष्परजोध्वस्ताम् समदामिव च क्वचित्
verses.iast:
kvacitkumudaśhṇḍaiśca kuḍmalairupaśobhitām |
nānāpuśhparajodhvastām samadāmiva ca kvacit
verses.translation: At some places, it was graced with beds of water lilies in the form of buds and at some places, it was reddened with the pollen of numerous flowers, as though excited with passion.

glosses.meaning: reddened with the pollen of numerous flowers

verses.devanagari:
व्यपेतमलसम्घाताम् मणिनिर्मलदर्शनाम् |
दिशागजैर्वनगजैर्मत्तैश्च वरवारणैः
देवोपवाह्यश्च मुहुः सम्नादितवनान्तराम् |
verses.iast:
vyapetamalasamghātām maṇinirmaladarśanām |
diśāgajairvanagajairmattaiśca varavāraṇaiḥ
devopavāhyaśca muhuḥ samnāditavanāntarām |
verses.translation: Having every aggregation of dirt removed, the river presented a spotlessly clear appearance like a crystal. The interior of the forest was reddened noisy again and again by the elephants guarding the quarters, by the ruttiest wild elephants and the elephants of excellent breed used for riding by gods.

glosses.meaning: having every aggregation of dirt removed
presenting a spotlessly clear appearance like a crystal
the interior of the forest rendered noisy
by the elephants guarding the quarters

verses.devanagari:
प्रमदामिव यत्ने न भूषिताम् भूषणोत्तमैः
फलैः पुष्पैः किसलयैर्वऋताम् गुल्मैद्द्विजैस्तथा |
शिंशुमरैः च नक्रैः च भुजम्गैः च निषेविताम्
verses.iast:
pramadāmiva yatne na bhūśhitām bhūśhaṇottamaiḥ
phalaiḥ puśhpaiḥ kisalayairvaṛtām gulmaiddvijaistathā |
śiṃśumaraiḥ ca nakraiḥ ca bhujamgaiḥ ca niṣevitām
verses.translation: Surrounded by fruits and flowers and tender leaves, shrubs and birds, it looked like a young woman artistically decked with the best of jewels. The river was infested with dolphins, crocodiles and snakes.

glosses.meaning: it looked like a young woman
the best of jewels. nishhevitaam = infested with

verses.devanagari:
विष्णुपादच्युताम् दिव्यामपापाम् पापनाशिनीम् |
ताम् शङ्करजटाजूटाद्भ्रष्टाम् सागरतेजसा
समुद्रमहीषीम् गङ्गाम् सारसक्रौञ्चनादिताम् |
आससाद महाबाहुः शृङ्गिबेरपुरम् प्रति
verses.iast:
viśhṇupādacyutām divyāmapāpām pāpanāśinīm |
tām śaṇ^karajaṭājūṭādbhraśhṭām sāgaratejasā
samudramahīśhīm gaṇ^gām sārasakrauJṇcanāditām |
āsasāda mahābāhuḥ śṛṇ^giberapuram prati
verses.translation: Rama, the mighty armed, reached the river Ganga, which is devoid of sins and which dispels all sins, which had fallen from the mass of matted hair of Lord Shankara through the spiritual power of Emperor Bhagiratha, which is rendered noisy by cranes and herons, which is a consort of the ocean and which is in the vicinity of Sringaverapura(the modern Singraur).

glosses.meaning: which flows from the feet of Lord Vishnu
from the mass of matted hair of Lord Shankara
through the spiritual power of the descendent of Sagara(Emperor Bhagiratha)
which was rendered noisy by cranes and herons
in the vicinity of Sringaverapura( the modern Singraur.)

verses.devanagari:
ताम् ऊर्मि कलिल आवर्ताम् अन्ववेक्ष्य महा रथः |
सुमन्त्रम् अब्रवीत् सूतम् इह एव अद्य वसामहे
verses.iast:
tām ūrmi kalila āvartām anvavekṣya mahā rathaḥ |
sumantram abravīt sūtam iha eva adya vasāmahe
verses.translation: Beholding the river Ganga with its waves covering whirlpools, Rama the great warrior said to Sumantra the charioteer as follows: "We shall halt here itself today."

verses.devanagari:
अविदूरात् अयम् नद्या बहु पुष्प प्रवालवान् |
सुमहान् इन्गुदी वृक्षो वसामः अत्र एव सारथे
verses.iast:
avidūrāt ayam nadyā bahu puṣpa pravālavān |
sumahān ingudī vṛkṣo vasāmaḥ atra eva sārathe
verses.translation: "Oh, charioteer! Not far from the river stands this very large sacred fig tree with its many flowers and shoots. We shall stay here itself."

glosses.meaning: with many flowers and shoots. VasaamaH = (We) shall stay

verses.devanagari:
द्रक्ष्यामः सरिताम् श्रेष्ठाम् सम्मान्यसलिलाम् शिवाम् |
देवदानवगन्धर्वमृगमानुषपक्षिणाम्
verses.iast:
drakśyāmaḥ saritām śreśhṭhām sammānyasalilām śivām |
devadānavagandharvamṛgamānuśhapakśiṇām
verses.translation: "I shall see (from here) the excellent river Ganga, which is auspicious and whose waters deserve to be respected by gods, men, Gandharvas, beasts, reptiles and birds ."

glosses.itrans: deva daanava gandharva mR^iga maanushha pakshhiNaam
glosses.iast: deva dānava gandharva mṛga mānuśha pakśhiṇām
glosses.devanagari: देव दानव गन्धर्व मृग मानुश्ह पक्श्हिणां

verses.devanagari:
लक्षणः च सुमन्त्रः च बाढम् इति एव राघवम् |
उक्त्वा तम् इन्गुदी वृक्षम् तदा उपययतुर् हयैः
verses.iast:
lakṣaṇaḥ ca sumantraḥ ca bāḍham iti eva rāghavam |
uktvā tam ingudī vṛkṣam tadā upayayatur hayaiḥ
verses.translation: Saying �so be it' and nothing more to Rama, Lakshmana and Sumantra too then directed the horses to that sacred fig tree.

verses.devanagari:
रामः अभियाय तम् रम्यम् वृक्षम् इक्ष्वाकु नन्दनः |
रथात् अवातरत् तस्मात् सभार्यः सह लक्ष्मणः
verses.iast:
rāmaḥ abhiyāya tam ramyam vṛkṣam ikṣvāku nandanaḥ |
rathāt avātarat tasmāt sabhāryaḥ saha lakṣmaṇaḥ
verses.translation: Rama, the delight of Ikshvaku dynasty, reached that beautiful tree and got down from the chariot along with Sita and Lakshmana.

verses.devanagari:
सुमन्त्रः अपि अवतीर्य एव मोचयित्वा हय उत्तमान् |
वृक्ष मूल गतम् रामम् उपतस्थे कृत अन्जलिः
verses.iast:
sumantraḥ api avatīrya eva mocayitvā haya uttamān |
vṛkṣa mūla gatam rāmam upatasthe kṛta anjaliḥ
verses.translation: Sumantra too dismounted from the chariot, unyoked the superb horses after which with joined palms, he seated himself near Rama at the foot of the tree.

glosses.meaning: at the foot of the tree.

verses.devanagari:
तत्र राजा गुहो नाम रामस्य आत्म समः सखा |
निषाद जात्यो बलवान् स्थपतिः च इति विश्रुतः
verses.iast:
tatra rājā guho nāma rāmasya ātma samaḥ sakhā |
niṣāda jātyo balavān sthapatiḥ ca iti viśrutaḥ
verses.translation: There, a king named Guha was Rama's friend dear to him as his own life. He was Nishada by birth, a strong man and well known as a ruler of Nishadas.

verses.devanagari:
स श्रुत्वा पुरुष व्याघ्रम् रामम् विषयम् आगतम् |
वृद्धैः परिवृतः अमात्यैः ज्ञातिभिः च अपि उपागतः
verses.iast:
sa śrutvā puruṣa vyāghram rāmam viṣayam āgatam |
vṛddhaiḥ parivṛtaḥ amātyaiḥ GYātibhiḥ ca api upāgataḥ
verses.translation: Hearing of Rama the tiger among men having come to his territory, he approached the prince, escorted by elderly ministers and relatives.

verses.devanagari:
ततः निषाद अधिपतिम् दृष्ट्वा दूरात् अवस्थितम् |
सह सौमित्रिणा रामः समागच्चद् गुहेन सः
verses.iast:
tataḥ niṣāda adhipatim dṛṣṭvā dūrāt avasthitam |
saha saumitriṇā rāmaḥ samāgaccad guhena saḥ
verses.translation: Seeing from a distance the king of Nishada coming, Rama along with Lakshmana thereupon went forth to meet Guha.

verses.devanagari:
तम् आर्तः सम्परिष्वज्य गुहो राघवम् अब्रवीत् |
यथा अयोध्या तथा इदम् ते राम किम् करवाणि ते
ईदृशम् हि महाबाहो कः प्रप्स्यत्यतिथिम् प्रियम् |
verses.iast:
tam ārtaḥ sampariṣvajya guho rāghavam abravīt |
yathā ayodhyā tathā idam te rāma kim karavāṇi te
īdṛśam hi mahābāho kaḥ prapsyatyatithim priyam |
verses.translation: Closely embracing Rama, Guha who felt disturbed, spoke to him, "This city too is as much as Ayodhya to you. What can I do for you? Oh mighty armed! Who indeed will get such a lovely guest?"

verses.devanagari:
ततः गुणवद् अन्न अद्यम् उपादाय पृथग् विधम् |
अर्घ्यम् च उपानयत् क्षिप्रम् वाक्यम् च इदम् उवाच ह
verses.iast:
tataḥ guṇavad anna adyam upādāya pṛthag vidham |
arghyam ca upānayat kṣipram vākyam ca idam uvāca ha
verses.translation: Having brought pristine cooked rice of excellent quality and other dishes of various kinds, he then quickly offered him water to wash his hands and spoke as follows:

glosses.meaning: and other dishes of various kinds

verses.devanagari:
स्वागतम् ते महा बाहो तव इयम् अखिला मही |
वयम् प्रेष्या भवान् भर्ता साधु राज्यम् प्रशाधि नः
verses.iast:
svāgatam te mahā bāho tava iyam akhilā mahī |
vayam preṣyā bhavān bhartā sādhu rājyam praśādhi naḥ
verses.translation: "Welcome to you, Oh, mighty armed! All this land is yours. We are your servants. You are the Lord. Rule over our kingdom in an efficient way."

glosses.meaning: are the Lord. Prashaadhi = Rule over

verses.devanagari:
भक्ष्यम् भोज्यम् च पेयम् च लेह्यम् च इदम् उपस्थितम् |
शयनानि च मुख्यानि वाजिनाम् खादनम् च ते
verses.iast:
bhakṣyam bhojyam ca peyam ca lehyam ca idam upasthitam |
śayanāni ca mukhyāni vājinām khādanam ca te
verses.translation: "Here have arrived various kinds of dishes, drinks and syrups as also excellent beds (for you to sleep on) and food for your horses"

verses.devanagari:
गुहम् एव ब्रुवाणम् तम् राघवः प्रत्युवाच ह
अर्चिताः चैव हृष्टाः च भवता सर्वथा वयम् |
पद्भ्याम् अभिगमाच् चैव स्नेह संदर्शनेन च
verses.iast:
guham eva bruvāṇam tam rāghavaḥ pratyuvāca ha
arcitāḥ caiva hṛṣṭāḥ ca bhavatā sarvathā vayam |
padbhyām abhigamāc caiva sneha saṃdarśanena ca
verses.translation: To Guha who was speaking as aforesaid, Rama replied thus: "We stand honored by you, by your very visit to us on foot, as well as your show of affection and are pleased with you"

glosses.meaning: as well as your show of affection

verses.devanagari:
भुजाभ्याम् साधु वृत्ताभ्याम् पीडयन् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् |
दिष्ट्या त्वाम् गुह पश्यामिअरोगम् सह बान्धवैः
अपि ते कूशलम् राष्ट्रे मित्रेषु च धनेषु च |
verses.iast:
bhujābhyām sādhu vṛttābhyām pīḍayan vākyam abravīt |
diṣṭyā tvām guha paśyāmiarogam saha bāndhavaiḥ
api te kūśalam rāṣṭre mitreṣu ca dhaneṣu ca |
verses.translation: Pressing gently with his muscular arms, Rama spoke these words: " Oh, Guha! Thank heaven that I am seeing you in good health with your relatives. Is all well with the kingdom, the allies and the treasure?"

verses.devanagari:
यत् तु इदम् भवता किंचित् प्रीत्या समुपकल्पितम् |
सर्वम् तत् अनुजानामि न हि वर्ते प्रतिग्रहे
verses.iast:
yat tu idam bhavatā kiṃcit prītyā samupakalpitam |
sarvam tat anujānāmi na hi varte pratigrahe
verses.translation: "I know your affection by which all this is extensively well arranged by you. But I am not in a position indeed to accept it."

glosses.meaning: by you. na varte hi = I am not in a condition indeed to

verses.devanagari:
कुश चीर अजिन धरम् फल मूल अशनम् च माम् |
विद्धि प्रणिहितम् धर्मे तापसम् वन गोचरम्
verses.iast:
kuśa cīra ajina dharam phala mūla aśanam ca mām |
viddhi praṇihitam dharme tāpasam vana gocaram
verses.translation: "Know me as under a vow to be an ascetic, wearing the robes of bark and deerskin and by piety, I am determined to live in the forest by eating roots and fruits only."

glosses.meaning: wearing the robes of bark and deerskin

verses.devanagari:
अश्वानाम् खादनेन अहम् अर्थी न अन्येन केनचित् |
एतावता अत्र भवता भविष्यामि सुपूजितः
verses.iast:
aśvānām khādanena aham arthī na anyena kenacit |
etāvatā atra bhavatā bhaviṣyāmi supūjitaḥ
verses.translation: "I desire nothing but a little forage for the horses. By being provided with this much at the present moment, I shall be duly satisfied by you."

glosses.meaning: and any other else. Etaavataa = by this much only

verses.devanagari:
एते हि दयिता राज्ञः पितुर् दशरथस्य मे |
एतैः सुविहितैः अश्वैः भविष्याम्य् अहम् अर्चितः
verses.iast:
ete hi dayitā rāGYaḥ pitur daśarathasya me |
etaiḥ suvihitaiḥ aśvaiḥ bhaviṣyāmy aham arcitaḥ
verses.translation: "These horses were cherished by the king Dasaratha, my father. I shall feel honored by these horses being duly fed."

verses.devanagari:
अश्वानाम् प्रतिपानम् च खादनम् चैव सो अन्वशात् |
गुहः तत्र एव पुरुषांस् त्वरितम् दीयताम् इति
verses.iast:
aśvānām pratipānam ca khādanam caiva so anvaśāt |
guhaḥ tatra eva puruṣāṃs tvaritam dīyatām iti
verses.translation: Then Guha on that spot commanded his men as follows: "Let water for drinking and forage be supplied promptly to horses"

verses.devanagari:
ततः चीर उत्तर आसन्गः संध्याम् अन्वास्य पश्चिमाम् |
जलम् एव आददे भोज्यम् लक्ष्मणेन आहृतम् स्वयम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ cīra uttara āsangaḥ saṃdhyām anvāsya paścimām |
jalam eva ādade bhojyam lakṣmaṇena āhṛtam svayam
verses.translation: Having worshipped the evening twilight appearing in the west, with an upper garment made of bark(on his person); Rama then took for food only water brought by Lakshmana himself.

glosses.meaning: the evening twilight appearing in the west
with an upper garment made of bark

verses.devanagari:
तस्य भूमौ शयानस्य पादौ प्रक्षाल्य लक्ष्मणः |
सभार्यस्य ततः अभ्येत्य तस्थौ वृष्कम् उपाश्रितः
verses.iast:
tasya bhūmau śayānasya pādau prakṣālya lakṣmaṇaḥ |
sabhāryasya tataḥ abhyetya tasthau vṛṣkam upāśritaḥ
verses.translation: Having washed the feet of Rama who was lying on the ground along with his consort, Lakshmana then came and stood near a tree.

verses.devanagari:
गुहो अपि सह सूतेन सौमित्रिम् अनुभाषयन् |
अन्वजाग्रत् ततः रामम् अप्रमत्तः धनुर् धरः
verses.iast:
guho api saha sūtena saumitrim anubhāṣayan |
anvajāgrat tataḥ rāmam apramattaḥ dhanur dharaḥ
verses.translation: Guha too along with the charioteer conversed with Lakshmana and thereafter wielding a bow; alertly kept a vigil over Rama.

verses.devanagari:
तथा शयानस्य ततः अस्य धीमतः |
यशस्विनो दाशरथेर् महात्मनः |
अदृष्ट दुह्खस्य सुख उचितस्य सा |
तदा व्यतीयाय चिरेण शर्वरी
verses.iast:
tathā śayānasya tataḥ asya dhīmataḥ |
yaśasvino dāśarather mahātmanaḥ |
adṛṣṭa duhkhasya sukha ucitasya sā |
tadā vyatīyāya cireṇa śarvarī
verses.translation: The illustrious, lofty minded and the high-soled son of Dasaratha, who had never seen suffering and who deserved all comforts, remained lying on the ground thereafter, while that long night passed away.
